name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 400 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 400 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces seized a Kuki-Zo camp in Manipur, arrested 17 suspects for impersonating SoO cadres and confiscated a large arms cache while chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh urged surrender of illegal weapons and linked gun culture to the violence. Kashmir IGP called for action against overground workers and hybrid terrorists, urging police to become more intelligence driven. Congress demanded the resignation of the Manipur chief minister, fresh elections and dissolution of the assembly. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker beslagla en Kuki-Zo-leir i Manipur, arresterte 17 mistenkte for å ha utgitt seg for SoO-kader og konfiskerte en stor våpenbeholdning, mens statsminister Yumnam Khemchand Singh oppfordret til overgivelse av illegale våpen og knyttet skytevåpenkulturen til volden. IGP i Kashmir oppfordret til handling mot overgrunnsarbeidere og hybride terrorister, og ba politiet bli mer etterretningsdrevet. Kongressen krevde at statsministeren i Manipur går av, nye valg og oppløsning av forsamlingen. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
